jobs.description:
A quantitative degree, a head for numbers, and a Brussels company where the calculations are the product.

Data Specialist | Brussels-Centre

Our client is an independent Belgian company active in specialised financial services, whose entire business rests on complex calculation models applied to long-term commitments.

What makes it stand out? A human-sized structure with the backing of a large group: entrepreneurial pace, short decision lines, and real proximity to the people who decide.

Its platforms are built and maintained in-house. Calculation engines, projections and regulatory reporting all run on proprietary applications, where the mathematical accuracy of the output comes before everything else.

To support its growth, the company is looking for a profile that combines quantitative work with business analysis, to help improve its internal systems.

The job

• Analyse the calculation rules and data behind the in-house applications, and turn what you find into concrete improvements to those systems.
• Act as a bridge between the business teams and the developers, translating quantitative needs into something that can be built.Role
• Model and test calculation rules, including edge cases, thresholds and exceptions, and identify where the systems can be improved.
• Verify the results produced by the applications: independent recalculations, consistency checks and investigation of discrepancies.
• Gather and challenge business needs, translate them into clear functional requirements, and take part in testing and validating what is delivered.
• Document the models, assumptions and implementation choices made.
Profile
• Master’s degree in a strongly quantitative field: mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, physics, civil engineering or equivalent. This is a firm requirement.
• Around 2 to 3 years of experience in a quantitative, analytical or business analysis role. Strong command of Excel is essential; knowledge of SQL, Python, R or VBA is an asset.
• French or Dutch with a basic knowledge of the other; English is a plus.

jobs.description:
Are you a true foodie who has always dreamed of working in the food industry?

Do you have experience in production and are you ready to turn your passion for snacks into a career? Then we are looking for you!

As a production hero at our food company, you will be responsible for producing the tastiest snacks available.

From mixing the perfect ingredients to controlling the production process, you are the key to our success.

You think it is something for you?

Call Konvert Food Roeselare on the number 051 24 56 29

What we expect from our new production hero:
 

 
• Experience in food production is a plus! (School leavers are also possible!!)
 
• Problem-solving ability
 
• Passion for good food and an eye for quality
 
• Willingness to work in night shift (21h-5h)
 
• Fluent knowledge of English!

What type of breed are we looking for? 
 

Our D2C channel is where we meet pet parents directly. No middleman, no shelf to fight for. It's how we build real relationships with the people (and pets) who love our food.
 

And it's not a side project. Our webshop is a serious business in its own right, representing a significant share of everything we sell, with a subscription base, a real tech team behind it, and years of compounding growth already on the clock. You'd be stepping into something that works, with the mandate to make it considerably bigger.
 

We're looking for a 
D2C & Digital Product Manager to own the roadmap that gets us there. You'll lead our Digital Product Team (2 full stack developers, a data engineer and product designer) and report directly to our Head of D2C.
 

You won't own the P&L. You'll own the roadmap that drives it, which in practice means you decide what we build, in what order, and why.
 

What is in your bowl? 
 

Own the roadmap that drives the channel
 

You decide what we build next and what waits. That means holding a clear point of view on where the growth actually is, translating it into a prioritised roadmap, and defending it when six good ideas arrive in the same week. You'll be measured on whether the channel grows profitably and sustainably, not on how many things got shipped.
 

Turn first-time buyers into a pack that stays
 

First purchase, subscription, loyalty. That's the journey, and it's yours to design end to end. Every step where a pet parent hesitates, churns, or quietly stops caring is a step you get to fix. CAC, LTV, AOV, retention and variable margin are the scoreboard, and CRM is one of your sharpest tools for moving them.
 

Own the campaign calendar
 

Product launches, seasonal moments, always-on lifecycle flows. You plan them, build them with your team, run them, and evaluate them honestly afterwards, together with Brand and Media.
 

Lead a team of four by example
 

Two full stack developers, one data engineer, one product designer. You'll set the direction, protect their focus, coach them, and raise the bar on craft. You won't be doing their jobs, but they should never feel like they're building for someone who doesn't understand what they do.
 

Keep us ahead on new technology
 

Including AI, and including whatever comes after it. You'll have an opinion on which new tools genuinely change the work and which ones are noise, and you'll put the useful ones in front of the team rather than in a deck.
 

Our stack 
 

We've built a headless shop on 
React + Shopify, with 
Klaviyo for CRM and lifecycle and 
Contentful for content. We design in 
Figma and the team runs on 
Notion. You don't need to have used all of it. You do need to be genuinely at home in a modern digital stack.

You're commercial to the bone. You can look at a roadmap and say which item moves LTV and which one just moves a ticket to Done. You've lived with numbers like CAC, AOV, variable margin, retention and forecast accuracy, and when one of them slips you know which lever to reach for.
 

You're hands-on in the engine room. You write the copy for the test yourself rather than waiting three weeks for a copywriter. You click through the feature before it ships. When the data doesn't explain the behaviour, you call a customer. Not because nobody else will, but because you want to know.
 

You've led a team of strong individual contributors. Developers, designers, data people. Specialists who are better at their craft than you are, and who can tell within a week whether you actually respect it. You've given them direction and honest feedback, protected their focus, and helped them get better at what they do. You'll be leading four of them from day one, so this one matters.
 

You live in the middle of Marketing, Design and Technology. You're as comfortable debating a campaign angle as you are reviewing a prototype or talking through a data model with an engineer. Those three worlds meeting is where you do your best work.
 

You prioritise like saying yes has a cost. Because it does. There will always be more good ideas than capacity, and you're the one who decides. You're comfortable being the person who says not this quarter, and explaining why.
 

You build brands, not discounts. You've seen what promo-led growth does to a business over time, and it doesn't excite you. What excites you is a customer who comes back because they love the thing, not because it was 20% off.
 

You know CRM is a craft, not a send button. You've built lifecycle programmes where the timing, the segment and the message all earned their place. You can tell relevant communication from noise, and so can your customers.
 

You get people around you moving without needing the org chart. Brand, Media & Partnerships, Logistics and Finance all have their own plans. You create clarity, you build the shared one, and people follow it because it makes sense.
 

You care about pets. Edgard and Cooper were real dogs, and everything we make still starts from one question: is this actually good for the animal eating it? You need to care about that answer. Ideally you live with a cat or a dog yourself and know exactly how it feels when the food runs out on a Sunday evening. For us this is essential, not a nice-to-have.
 

You bring 5+ years of experience in D2C, e-commerce or digital product, and you're 
fluent in Dutch and English.

jobs.occupation: Researcher - PhD Candidate in Political Economy / International Relations (FRACTURE) M/W/X
jobs.description:
MAIN TASKS

• Conduct doctoral research in international relations, defence policy and international security.
• Develop the theoretical framework of the project, including an extensive review of the literature on alliances, strategic alignment, great-power competition and cooperation among revisionist powers.
• Collect, structure and analyse quantitative and qualitative data concerning the relations among China, Russia, Iran and North Korea.
• Develop a dataset covering cooperation in several domains, including economic, diplomatic, military and technological relations.
• Apply network analysis techniques to map and analyse the structure and evolution of cooperation among the four states.
• Produce network visualisations and quantitative indicators identifying patterns, central actors and asymmetries.
• Conduct qualitative and comparative case studies of episodes of cooperation, competition and geopolitical tension.
• Analyse the political, economic and strategic drivers of cooperation as well as structural asymmetries, dependencies and potential vulnerabilities.
• Contribute to scientific publications, working papers, policy briefs, blog posts and other dissemination outputs.
• Present research results at international academic conferences, RMA seminars and Defence-oriented events.
• Contribute to the activities of relevant academic and institutional research networks, including NATO-related research activities.
• Support knowledge transfer between academic research and Belgian Defence stakeholders.v 
SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Degree required / ideal degree:

Master's degree in Economics, Political Economy, International Relations, Political Science, or a related field.

This position is open to junior or early-career researchers (0-3 years of experience).

The position is intended for a researcher interested in pursuing a PhD trajectory within the framework of the FRACTURE project.

 

MUST HAVE

• Strong background in political economy, international relations, or related fields 
• Ability to analyse complex geopolitical and international security issues.
• Strong analytical and academic writing skills.
• Ability and motivation to conduct independent scientific research.
• Interest in both quantitative and qualitative research methods.
 

NICE TO HAVE

• Experience with network analysis / data analysis tools (e.g. R, Python, Gephi, etc.) 
• Knowledge of the foreign and security policies of China, Russia, Iran and/or North Korea.
• Familiarity with alliance theory, strategic studies or defence policy.
• Experience working with international economic, diplomatic or security-related datasets.
• Experience with qualitative case-study research.
• Experience with policy-oriented or Defence-related research.
• Experience writing policy briefs or communicating research to non-academic audiences.
 

PERSONAL SKILLS

• Ability to work independently in a multidisciplinary research environment 
• Analytical, critical, and creative thinking 
• Clear and effective communication (oral and written) 
• Proactive, organized, and result-oriented 
• Strong team spirit and collaboration skills 
• High level of integrity and confidentiality
 

OTHER SKILLS

• Excellent command of English (oral and written) 
• Knowledge of French and/or Dutch is an asset 
 

SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS

• The researcher may be exposed to classified information and will therefore have to obtain the required security clearance. The candidate must consent with the background check required to obtain this clearance, which will be executed by Belgian Defence.
• Working for the Patrimony requires living in Belgium for the duration of the study.
 
 
CONTRACT

• Probable date of recruitment: From March 1st, 2027, in consultation with the applicant. 
• Status: Full-time employment based on an open-ended contract with the Patrimony of the Royal Military Academy (you will not be a civil servant). Please note that your contract will be open-ended, but the financing of the contract will be tied to the funding project, which is guaranteed until 28/02/2031.
• Wage scale: class NA11 (holder of a Master's degree), with valuable/relevant seniority. A salary simulation can be done here : Simulateur de salaire. RMA-Patrimony applies a merit-based research career track, allowing researchers to advance in wage scale based upon annual evaluations.
• 
Holiday pay.

 

EXTRA LEGAL BENEFITS

• Possibility to benefit from a bilingualism allowance (Dutch/French) following a SELOR test;
• End-of-year bonus;
• Free DKV hospitalization insurance. Possibility of additional affiliation for one or more persons living under the same roof: spouse, child(ren) (50% of the price per additional member);
• Bike allowance / Free public transport (home-work commute);
• Meal vouchers (6€ / day);
• Digital allowance (15€ / month);
• Free access to campus sports facilities outside working hours;
• On-campus restaurant and cafeteria with democratic prices (discount on the daily menu);
• Flexible working hours within the 38-hour week;
• Teleworking possible with allowance (2 days / week max);
• Holidays: 
• 29 days holiday / year from the 1st year of contract (then from 45 years: +1 day holiday every 5 years) 
• 1 week OFF every year between Christmas and New year's Eve (independent of the annual balance of holidays).
• Advantages and interesting offers thanks to the Benefits@work card (discounts, vouchers...);
• Entitlement to services offered by the `Office Central d'Action Sociale et Culturelle de la Défense' (OCASC): among others holiday centres, discount on travel organised by the tour operator...;
• Possibility to benefit from the nursery funded by Belgian Defence (subject to availability).
